Exercise A

Maria's Life in Alaska

Read the text carefully, then answer the questions below.

Read the text

Maria is fifteen years old and lives in Anchorage, Alaska — the biggest city in America's largest state. Alaska is in the far northwest of the USA. It is famous for its mountains, forests and wild animals like bears, moose and bald eagles.

Maria's school has a social project called "Clean Alaska". Every month, the students go to a beach or a park and collect rubbish. They pick up plastic bottles, bags and old cans. Maria says: "It is important because animals can eat the rubbish and get sick."

At school, Maria learned about the product life cycle. A product life cycle shows what happens to a product from start to finish. First, raw materials are collected. Then, the product is made in a factory. After that, it is sold in shops and used by people. Finally, the product is thrown away or recycled. Maria thinks recycling is very important because it helps the environment.

Last month, Maria and her class volunteered at a wildlife centre in Anchorage. They helped feed baby birds and clean the animal cages. Maria loves working with animals. She says: "Volunteering is fun and you learn a lot. I enjoy helping animals because they cannot help themselves."

Answer the questions
1. Where does Maria live?
2. What is Alaska famous for?
3. What do the students collect during "Clean Alaska"?
4. What is the first step in a product life cycle?
5. Where did Maria volunteer last month?
6. Why does Maria enjoy volunteering?
Exercise B

Passive Voice — Simple Present

Complete each sentence with the correct passive form. Think about whether the subject is singular or plural.

Grammar reminder

We use the passive voice when the action is more important than who does it.

Form: am / is / are + past participle (3rd form)

Active: Workers make plastic bottles. → Passive: Plastic bottles are made by workers.

Singular: The cake is baked every morning.
Plural: The cakes are baked every morning.

Fill in the gaps
1. Plastic bottles _____ in factories every day. (make)
2. Rubbish _____ by students during "Clean Alaska". (collect)
3. Old paper _____ to the recycling centre every week. (take)
4. Baby birds at the wildlife centre _____ three times a day. (feed)
5. The beaches in Alaska _____ by volunteers every month. (clean)
6. New products _____ in shops all over the world. (sell)
7. Alaska _____ by millions of tourists every year. (visit)
8. The animal cages _____ by the students every morning. (wash)
Exercise C

Gerunds — The -ing Form as a Noun

Choose the correct gerund (-ing form) to complete each sentence.

Grammar reminder

A gerund is the -ing form of a verb used as a noun.

As subject: Swimming is fun. / Reading books is my hobby.

After certain verbs: enjoy, like, love, hate, stop, finish, keep, avoid, suggest
I enjoy reading. / She finished cooking.

Fill in the gaps
1. _____ rubbish on the beach is very important. (collect)
2. Maria enjoys _____ at the wildlife centre. (work)
3. _____ in cold water is exciting but dangerous. (swim)
4. The students finished _____ the park at 3 p.m. (clean)
5. Maria keeps _____ about her volunteer work. (talk)
6. We should avoid _____ plastic bags. (use)
7. _____ about product life cycles helps you understand recycling. (learn)
8. The volunteers suggested _____ the beach every weekend. (visit)
Exercise D

Writing — Volunteering & Social Projects

Write two short paragraphs (6–8 sentences total). Use at least two passive sentences and at least two gerunds.

What to write

Paragraph 1 — A social project: Describe a social project at your school or in your town. What is done? Who helps? What is collected or cleaned?

Paragraph 2 — Volunteering: Would you like to volunteer? What kind of volunteering do you enjoy? Why is helping others important?

Helpful phrases
Passive voice: Rubbish is collected… Trees are planted… Old clothes are donated… Food is prepared… The park is cleaned…
Gerunds: Helping others is… I enjoy volunteering… Collecting rubbish… Working together… Recycling is important…
